questions.stem: A and B are partners. A advanced a loan of ₹2,00,000 to the firm on 1st October 2024. The firm incurred a net loss of ₹30,000 before interest. The partnership deed is silent on interest on loan. What amount of interest is payable to A and where is it credited?
options: (a) Nil, because firm incurred a loss
questions.correctAnswer: (c) ₹6,000 credited to A's Loan Account
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Interest on loan is a charge @ 6% p.a. for 6 months (₹6,000) and credits Loan A/c.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Personal drawings of a partner against capital affect the calculation of interest on capital from the date of withdrawal.
Reason (R): Drawings against capital are debited to Partner's Capital Account, thereby reducing the capital balance.
options: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.rubric: 1 Mark for identifying capital withdrawal mechanism.

questions.stem: X, Y, and Z are partners sharing profits equally. Z withdraws ₹10,000 at the end of each quarter throughout the year. Interest on drawings is charged @ 10% p.a. The interest on Z's drawings will be:

A and B entered into partnership on 1st April 2024 contributing ₹5,00,000 and ₹3,00,000. The deed provides interest on capital @ 6% p.a. and partner salary to B of ₹5,000 per month. Net profit before appropriations was ₹48,000. How will the profit be distributed?
questions.rubric: Appropriation exceeds profit (Total claim: A IOC ₹30,000; B IOC ₹18,000 + Salary ₹60,000 = ₹78,000). Total claims ratio = 30,000 : 78,000 = 5 : 13 [1 Mark]. Available profit ₹48,000 distributed in 5:13 ratio: A = ₹13,333, B = ₹34,667 [2 Marks].

questions.stem: P and Q are partners with capitals of ₹6,00,000 and ₹4,00,000. On 31st March 2025, after closing books and crediting profit of ₹2,00,000, it was discovered that Interest on Capital @ 8% p.a. and Interest on Drawings of ₹12,000 (P) and ₹8,000 (Q) were omitted. Calculate opening capitals and pass the adjusting entry assuming capitals are fluctuating.
questions.correctAnswer: Adjusting Journal Entry: Q's Capital A/c Dr. to P's Capital A/c ₹2,000
questions.rubric: Calculation of Opening Capital [1 Mark]. Table showing adjustments [1 Mark]. Journal entry with narration [1 Mark].

questions.stem: M, N, and O are partners sharing profits in 3:2:1. O is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹30,000 p.a. Firm's profit for the year ended 31st March 2025 was ₹1,20,000. Prepare Profit and Loss Appropriation Account if any deficiency is to be borne by M and N in the ratio of 2:1.
questions.rubric: Normal shares: M ₹60,000; N ₹40,000; O ₹20,000 [1 Mark]. Deficiency of O = ₹10,000 borne by M (₹6,667) and N (₹3,333) [1 Mark]. P&L Appropriation Account layout [1 Mark].

questions.stem: The capital balances of Anu, Binu, and Charu on 31st March 2025 stood at ₹2,50,000, ₹2,00,000, and ₹1,50,000 respectively. Profit of ₹90,000 for the year had been distributed equally without providing for: (i) Interest on capital @ 10% p.a., (ii) Salary to Anu ₹2,000 per month, (iii) Commission to Charu of ₹6,000. Pass a single adjusting journal entry showing working notes clearly.
questions.correctAnswer: Single adjusting entry debiting/crediting partner capital accounts
questions.rubric: Working table showing net adjustments [2.5 Marks]. Adjusting Journal Entry with correct narration [1.5 Marks].

questions.stem: Karan and Varun started business on 1st April 2024. Karan brought ₹4,00,000 as capital and Varun contributed ₹2,00,000 as capital alongside personal premises worth ₹10,000 monthly rent. Deed provided: (i) Interest on Capital @ 9% p.a., (ii) Karan to get 10% commission on net profit after charging such commission. Net profit before rent was ₹1,80,000. Prepare Profit & Loss Appropriation Account.
questions.correctAnswer: Net profit transferred to P&L App: ₹60,000
questions.rubric: Rent treated as charge in P&L A/c: ₹1,80,000 - ₹1,20,000 = ₹60,000 [1.5 Marks]. Interest on capital restricted to available profits [1.5 Marks]. Distribution in IOC ratio [1 Mark].

questions.stem: Three chartered accountants A, B, and C formed a partnership sharing profits in 2:2:1. C is guaranteed a minimum gross fee of ₹50,000 by the firm. In turn, A guarantees that gross fee earned by him for the firm shall not be less than ₹80,000. Actual fee earned by A was ₹62,000. Total profits before adjustments stood at ₹1,50,000. Prepare Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
questions.correctAnswer: Distributable profit ₹1,68,000 adjusted for guarantees
questions.rubric: A's shortfall ₹18,000 debited to A and credited to P&L App [2 Marks]. Total profit ₹1,68,000 distributed in 2:2:1 [2 Marks]. C's guarantee deficiency calculated and recovered from remaining partners [2 Marks].

questions.stem: Dev and Preet were partners. Balance Sheet on 31st March 2025 showed Capitals: Dev ₹5,00,000; Preet ₹3,00,000. During the year, Dev's drawings were ₹80,000 and Preet's drawings were ₹40,000. Net profit ₹1,60,000 was divided without providing 10% p.a. interest on capital and charging interest on drawings (Dev ₹4,000, Preet ₹2,000). Show working notes and pass single rectification entry if: (Case A) Capitals are Fixed, (Case B) Capitals are Fluctuating.
questions.correctAnswer: Case A adjusts Current A/cs; Case B calculates Opening Capital and adjusts Capital A/cs
questions.rubric: Case A (Fixed Capital) adjustment table and entry [3 Marks]. Case B (Fluctuating Capital) reverse opening capital table and entry [3 Marks].

questions.stem: A and B are partners. A advanced a loan of ₹3,00,000 to the firm on 1st October 2024. The firm incurred a net loss of ₹20,000 for the year ended 31st March 2025 before considering any interest. The partnership deed is silent on interest on loan. Which entry correctly reflects the interest treatment?
options: (a) Profit & Loss A/c Dr. ₹9,000 to A's Loan A/c ₹9,000
(b) Profit & Loss Appropriation A/c Dr. ₹9,000 to A's Capital A/c ₹9,000
(c) Profit & Loss A/c Dr. ₹9,000 to A's Capital A/c ₹9,000
(d) No entry is passed because the firm incurred a net loss
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Profit & Loss A/c Dr. ₹9,000 to A's Loan A/c ₹9,000
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Interest on partner's loan is a charge against profit under Sec 13(d) @ 6% p.a. (₹3,00,000 × 6% × 6/12 = ₹9,000). It must be debited to P&L A/c and credited to Partner's Loan A/c, never Capital A/c.

questions.stem: A partner withdrew ₹80,000 during the financial year. The partnership deed provides for interest on drawings @ 10% (without the word 'per annum'). The interest charged on drawings will be:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. When the suffix 'p.a.' is absent from the interest rate, interest is charged for the entire year irrespective of the date/duration of withdrawals (₹80,000 × 10% = ₹8,000).

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Under the Fixed Capital method, a partner's capital account balance can never show a debit balance.
Reason (R): All regular adjustments regarding interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings, and profit/loss share are credited or debited to the Partner's Current Account.
options: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Capital account under fixed method records only initial capital, additional capital, and permanent withdrawal of capital, maintaining a credit (or nil) balance.

questions.stem: Closing balance of X's Capital Account on 31st March 2025 was ₹6,00,000. During the year, his drawings against profits were ₹60,000, share of profit credited was ₹80,000, and he introduced additional capital of ₹1,50,000 on 1st October 2024. If the partners maintain Fixed Capitals, what was X's opening capital on 1st April 2024?
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Under Fixed Capital method, drawings against profits and annual profits are routed through Current Account. Opening Capital = Closing Capital (₹6,00,000) - Additional Capital (₹1,50,000) = ₹4,50,000.

questions.stem: A and B share profits in 3:1 with capitals of ₹3,00,000 and ₹1,00,000. The deed provides interest on capital @ 6% p.a. Net profit before interest for the year was ₹16,000. In the absence of an agreement treating IOC as a charge, how will the profit be distributed?
options: (c) A: ₹12,000; B: ₹4,000 with a net loss of ₹8,000
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Total IOC due = ₹18,000 + ₹6,000 = ₹24,000. Since available profit (₹16,000) is insufficient, profit is distributed in the ratio of claims (18,000:6,000 = 3:1). A gets ₹12,000, B gets ₹4,000.

questions.stem: A partner withdraws ₹6,000 on the 15th day of every month for the six months ending 31st March 2025. Interest on drawings is charged @ 12% p.a. The interest on drawings will be:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Total drawings = 6 × ₹6,000 = ₹36,000. Average period = (5.5 + 0.5) / 2 = 3 months. Interest = 36,000 × 12% × 3/12 = ₹1,080.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Rent paid to a partner for using his personal premises for business operations is debited to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
Reason (R): Any payment made to a partner as per the terms of partnership agreement constitutes an appropriation of divisible profit.
options: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
(d) Both A and R are false
questions.correctAnswer: (d) Both A and R are false
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Rent paid to a partner is a charge against profit (debited to P&L Account) because the partner acts as a landlord in an independent capacity, not as an owner.

questions.stem: Net profit before manager's commission is ₹1,32,000. Manager is entitled to 10% commission on net profits after charging such commission. Partner Z is entitled to a quarterly salary of ₹5,000. Net profit transferred to Profit & Loss Appropriation Account will be:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Manager's commission is a charge in P&L A/c: ₹1,32,000 × 10/110 = ₹12,000. Net profit transferred to P&L App = ₹1,32,000 - ₹12,000 = ₹1,20,000.

questions.stem:
Statement I: Interest on loan taken by a partner from the firm is credited to Profit and Loss Account.
Statement II: In the absence of an agreement, the firm can charge interest @ 6% p.a. on loans given to partners.
options: (c) Statement I is true, Statement II is false
(d) Statement I is false, Statement II is true
questions.correctAnswer: (c) Statement I is true, Statement II is false
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Interest on loan given to partner is business income (credited to P&L A/c). However, Sec 13 only prescribes 6% on loans given BY partners to the firm; firm cannot charge interest on loans given TO partners without an agreement.

questions.stem: P, Q, and R share profits in 5:3:2. R is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹25,000 by P. The firm earned a net profit of ₹1,50,000 for the year. What is the net profit share credited to P's Capital Account?
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. R's normal share = 2/10 × ₹1,50,000 = ₹30,000. Since R's actual share exceeds the guaranteed amount (₹30,000 > ₹25,000), there is zero deficiency. P receives his full share of ₹75,000.

questions.stem: A firm incurred a net loss of ₹30,000 during the year. The partnership deed provides for Interest on Capital of ₹25,000 and Interest on Drawings of ₹10,000. What is the net amount transferred to Partners' Capital Accounts?
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Net Loss of ₹20,000
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. In case of net loss, IOC is ignored. Interest on drawings (₹10,000) is credited against the loss of ₹30,000, leaving a net loss of ₹20,000 to be shared.

questions.stem: Partner M is entitled to a commission of 5% on net profit before charging any commission. Partner N is entitled to 5% on net profit after charging all commissions. Net profit before charging any commission is ₹2,10,000. What is N's commission?
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. M's commission = 5% of ₹2,10,000 = ₹10,500. Balance profit before N's commission = ₹2,10,000 - ₹10,500 = ₹1,99,500. N's commission = ₹1,99,500 × 5/105 = ₹9,500.

questions.stem: Partner K gave a loan of ₹1,00,000 on 1st July 2024 to the firm. Partner L took a loan of ₹60,000 from the firm on 1st October 2024. The partnership deed is silent on interest. Net profit before any loan adjustments was ₹50,000. Net profit transferred to P&L Appropriation A/c is:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Interest on K's loan = ₹1,00,000 × 6% × 9/12 = ₹4,500 (charge to P&L). In the absence of deed, firm cannot charge interest on loan taken by L. Net profit transferred = ₹50,000 - ₹4,500 = ₹45,500.

questions.stem: X and Y started business on 1st April 2024 contributing ₹4,00,000 and ₹6,00,000. On 1st July 2024, X introduced ₹2,00,000 while Y withdrew ₹1,00,000 from capital. If profits are shared in the effective capital-employed ratio, the profit-sharing ratio is:
A and B share profits in 2:1. On 31st March 2025, after dividing profit of ₹90,000, it was found that Interest on Capital @ 10% p.a. (A ₹15,000, B ₹10,000) was omitted. In the single adjusting entry:
options: (a) A's Capital A/c Dr. ₹1,667 to B's Capital A/c ₹1,667
(b) B's Capital A/c Dr. ₹1,667 to A's Capital A/c ₹1,667
(c) A's Capital A/c Dr. ₹5,000 to B's Capital A/c ₹5,000
(d) B's Capital A/c Dr. ₹5,000 to A's Capital A/c ₹5,000
questions.correctAnswer: (a) A's Capital A/c Dr. ₹1,667 to B's Capital A/c ₹1,667
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Omitted IOC total ₹25,000 credited (A +₹15,000, B +₹10,000). Wrong profit reversed in 2:1 (A -₹16,667, B -₹8,333). Net effect: A Net Dr. ₹1,667, B Net Cr. ₹1,667.

questions.stem: The partnership deed provides for interest on capital @ 9% p.a. as a charge against profits. Capital balances are ₹2,00,000 and ₹1,00,000. Net profit for the year is ₹18,000. The net result shown by P&L Account will be:
options: (a) Net profit ₹18,000 transferred to P&L App
(b) Net loss ₹9,000 transferred to Capital Accounts
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Net loss ₹9,000 transferred to Capital Accounts
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. When IOC is a charge, it is fully debited to P&L A/c regardless of profit: ₹27,000 IOC - ₹18,000 profit = ₹9,000 Net Loss.

questions.stem: V withdraws ₹12,000 at the end of each half-year. Interest on drawings is charged @ 10% p.a. What is the total interest charged for the year ending 31st March?
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Total drawings = 2 × ₹12,000 = ₹24,000. Average period = (6 + 0) / 2 = 3 months. Interest = 24,000 × 10% × 3/12 = ₹600.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Transfer to General Reserve is recorded on the debit side of Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
Reason (R): General reserve is created out of divisible profits to strengthen the financial position and is not a charge against current revenue.
options: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Transfer to reserve is an appropriation of profit, hence debited to P&L Appropriation Account.

questions.stem: Which of the following items is debited to Partner's Capital Account under the Fluctuating Capital method?
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Partner's share of Net Loss
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Share of net loss reduces partner's capital and is debited. Interest on loan goes to Loan A/c; commission and additional capital are credited.

questions.stem: A and B are partners sharing profits in 3:2. Deed provides for 10% p.a. interest on capital and salary of ₹2,000 p.m. to A. Net profit is ₹40,000. Total appropriations claim: IOC ₹20,000 and Salary ₹24,000. A's total receipt will be:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Total claims = ₹44,000 against available profit of ₹40,000. Claims ratio = (A's claim: IOC ₹12k + Salary ₹24k = ₹36k) : (B's claim: IOC ₹8k) = 36:8 = 9:2. A receives 9/11 × 40,000 = ₹32,727.

questions.stem: If drawings of equal amounts are made at the beginning of each quarter, the interest on total drawings is calculated for an average period of:
questions.correctAnswer: (c) 7.5 months
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Average period = (Months left after 1st drawing + Months left after last drawing) / 2 = (12 + 3) / 2 = 7.5 months.

questions.stem:
Statement I: A sleeping partner is liable to third parties for all debts of the firm.
Statement II: A sleeping partner is not entitled to inspect the books of accounts of the firm.
options: (b) Statement I is true, Statement II is false
(c) Statement I is false, Statement II is true
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Statement I is true, Statement II is false
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. All partners (including dormant/sleeping) have unlimited liability and possess the statutory right under Sec 12(d) to inspect and copy any book of the firm.

questions.stem: A partner withdraws ₹10,000 on 1st May 2024, ₹15,000 on 1st November 2024, and ₹5,000 on 28th February 2025. Rate of interest on drawings is 12% p.a. Accounts close on 31st March. Total interest on drawings is:
In the absence of a partnership deed, an active partner devoting his entire time to business operations is entitled to:
options: (d) Salary equal to lowest drawing limit
questions.correctAnswer: (c) No remuneration whatsoever
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Section 13(a) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 explicitly states that a partner is not entitled to receive any remuneration for taking part in the conduct of the business.

questions.stem: A and B share profits in 2:1. Net profit before interest on loan is ₹45,000. A provided a loan of ₹1,00,000 on 1st October 2024. B is entitled to a rent of ₹2,000 per month for firm premises. What is the net divisible profit transferred to P&L Appropriation Account?
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Both are charges against profit: Loan interest = 1,00,000 × 6% × 6/12 = ₹3,000; Rent = ₹24,000. Total charges = ₹27,000. Net profit transferred to P&L App = ₹45,000 - ₹27,000 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A, B, and C were partners in a firm sharing profits in 2:2:1. C was guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹40,000 p.a. by A and B equally. The firm earned a net profit of ₹75,000 for the year ended 31st March 2025. Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
questions.rubric: Normal shares: A ₹30,000; B ₹30,000; C ₹15,000 [1 Mark]. C's deficiency = ₹25,000 borne equally by A (₹12,500) and B (₹12,500) [1 Mark]. Final P&L Appropriation Account format [1 Mark].

questions.stem: X and Y are partners sharing profits in 3:2 with capitals of ₹5,00,000 and ₹3,00,000. Interest on capital is agreed @ 6% p.a. and Y is allowed an annual salary of ₹24,000. Net profit for the year before any appropriation was ₹36,000. Show the distribution of profit.
questions.rubric: Total claims exceed profit: X (IOC ₹30,000); Y (IOC ₹18,000 + Salary ₹24,000 = ₹42,000). Total claims ratio = 30,000 : 42,000 = 5:7 [1 Mark]. Available profit ₹36,000 distributed in 5:7: X = ₹15,000; Y = ₹21,000 [2 Marks].

questions.stem: R and S are partners. R's capital on 1st April 2024 was ₹4,00,000. On 1st October 2024, he introduced ₹1,00,000 as additional capital and withdrew ₹50,000 on 1st January 2025 against capital. Calculate interest on R's capital @ 8% p.a. for the year ended 31st March 2025.
questions.correctAnswer: Interest on Capital = ₹35,000
questions.rubric: 4,00,000 × 8% = ₹32,000 [1 Mark]. Additional capital: 1,00,000 × 8% × 6/12 = ₹4,000 [1 Mark]. Capital withdrawal reduction: 50,000 × 8% × 3/12 = (₹1,000) [0.5 Mark]. Total = ₹35,000 [0.5 Mark].

questions.stem: A partner withdrew ₹15,000 on 15th April, ₹12,000 on 30th June, ₹18,000 on 1st December, and ₹20,000 on 28th February. Books close on 31st March 2025. Calculate interest on drawings @ 9% p.a. using the product method.
questions.correctAnswer: Interest on Drawings = ₹2,794

questions.stem: Ankit, Bobby, and Kartik share profits in 4:3:3. After the accounts were closed on 31st March 2025, it was discovered that interest on drawings @ 6% p.a. was omitted. Drawings were: Ankit ₹40,000, Bobby ₹30,000, and Kartik ₹20,000 (dates not specified). Pass a single adjusting journal entry.
questions.correctAnswer: Adjusting Entry: Ankit's Capital A/c Dr. ₹120 to Bobby's Capital A/c ₹90, Kartik's Capital A/c ₹30
questions.rubric: Average 6 months interest: Ankit ₹1,200; Bobby ₹900; Kartik ₹600; Total = ₹2,700 [1 Mark]. Profit credit in 4:3:3 (Ankit ₹1,080; Bobby ₹810; Kartik ₹810) [1 Mark]. Net table and journal entry with narration [1 Mark].

questions.stem: P and Q are partners sharing profits in 3:2. On 1st April 2024, P advanced a loan of ₹1,50,000 to the firm. On the same date, Q took a loan of ₹1,00,000 from the firm. Agreement provides interest on loan taken by Q @ 8% p.a. Firm made a loss of ₹10,000 before interest. Prepare Profit & Loss Account.
questions.correctAnswer: Net Loss transferred to P&L App: ₹11,000
questions.rubric: Debit side: Initial loss ₹10,000 + Interest on P's loan (charge under Sec 13 @ 6% = ₹9,000) = ₹19,000 [1.5 Marks]. Credit side: Interest on Q's loan (income to firm = ₹8,000) [1 Mark]. Net loss transferred = ₹11,000 [0.5 Mark].

questions.stem: Kamal and Vimal are partners. Balance Sheet as at 31st March 2025 showed Capitals: Kamal ₹3,00,000; Vimal ₹2,00,000. Profits of ₹80,000 were divided without providing interest on capital @ 10% p.a. During the year, Kamal's drawings were ₹40,000 and Vimal's drawings were ₹20,000. Calculate opening capitals and interest on capital assuming capitals are fluctuating.
questions.correctAnswer: Opening Capitals: Kamal ₹3,00,000; Vimal ₹1,80,000. IOC: Kamal ₹30,000; Vimal ₹18,000
questions.rubric: Kamal Opening Capital = 3,00,000 + 40,000 - 40,000 = ₹3,00,000 [1 Mark]. Vimal Opening Capital = 2,00,000 + 20,000 - 40,000 = ₹1,80,000 [1 Mark]. IOC calculation @ 10% [1 Mark].

questions.stem: A, B, and C entered into partnership on 1st October 2024. A contributed ₹4,00,000, B ₹3,00,000, and C ₹2,00,000. Profit sharing ratio is 2:2:1. C is guaranteed minimum profit of ₹25,000 for the period ended 31st March 2025. Total firm profit was ₹60,000. Prepare Profit & Loss Appropriation Account.
questions.rubric: C's normal share for 6 months = 1/5 × ₹60,000 = ₹12,000 [1 Mark]. Deficiency = ₹25,000 - ₹12,000 = ₹13,000 borne by A and B equally (₹6,500 each) [1 Mark]. P&L Appropriation Account layout [1 Mark].

questions.stem: Simran and Reet are partners sharing profits in 3:2. Their Capital Account balances on 31st March 2025 were ₹4,50,000 and ₹3,00,000. It was found that interest on capital @ 8% p.a. was credited to them though the partnership deed was silent regarding interest on capital. Pass the necessary rectification entry.
questions.correctAnswer: Net effect is Nil (No entry required)
questions.rubric: Capital ratio is 4,50,000 : 3,00,000 = 3:2, which is identical to PSR. The credit of IOC and reversal in PSR cancel each other out. Explaining that net effect is Nil earns full marks [3 Marks].

questions.stem:
State the accounting treatment in the following independent cases:
(i) Partner Z gave a guarantee to the firm that gross fees earned by him will be ₹50,000, but he earned ₹38,000.
(ii) Firm incurred a net loss of ₹15,000, but partnership deed provides interest on capital of ₹20,000.
questions.correctAnswer: (i) Z's Capital A/c Dr. ₹12,000 to P&L Appropriation A/c; (ii) No Interest on Capital is allowed
questions.rubric: (i) Explanation and entry for recovery of partner's guarantee shortfall [1.5 Marks]. (ii) Explanation that IOC is an appropriation and cannot be allowed during a loss [1.5 Marks].

questions.stem: A and B were partners sharing profits in 3:2. Books for the year ended 31st March 2025 showed Net Profit ₹1,80,000. After finalization, it was discovered that: (i) Interest on Capital @ 8% p.a. was credited on closing capitals (A ₹6,00,000, B ₹4,00,000) instead of opening capitals; (ii) Drawings against profits were A ₹60,000 and B ₹40,000; (iii) A had introduced ₹1,00,000 as additional capital on 1st October 2024; (iv) Interest on drawings @ 10% p.a. was omitted. Pass a single adjusting journal entry showing reverse opening capital calculations.
questions.correctAnswer: Adjusting Journal Entry: B's Capital A/c Dr. ₹2,160 to A's Capital A/c ₹2,160

questions.stem: The Balance Sheet of X and Y as on 31st March 2025 showed: Capital A/cs: X ₹5,00,000, Y ₹3,00,000; General Reserve ₹1,20,000; P&L A/c (Cr. 2024-25) ₹80,000. On Asset side: Drawings A/c: X ₹40,000; Other Assets ₹9,60,000. Y's drawings of ₹30,000 were debited to his capital account. Profit of ₹1,60,000 for 2024-25 was divided without providing IOC @ 10% p.a. and Salary to X of ₹2,000 p.m. Calculate opening capitals and pass single rectifying entry.
questions.correctAnswer: Opening Capitals: X ₹4,60,000; Y ₹2,90,000. Single adjusting entry with workings.
questions.rubric: X's drawings shown on asset side means NOT deducted from Capital; profit credited in Capital = 1,60,000 - 80,000 in BS = ₹80,000 split (X ₹40k, Y ₹40k) [1.5 Marks]. questions.correctAnswer: P Commission: ₹33,000; Q Commission: ₹27,000; R Commission: ₹10,000

Deed provided: (i) IOC @ 10% p.a.; (ii) Salary to O ₹2,000 p.m. Prepare Profit & Loss Account, Profit & Loss Appropriation Account, and Partners' Capital Accounts.
questions.correctAnswer: P&L Net Profit ₹26,000; Claims ratio applied in P&L App
questions.rubric: P&L Account showing Rent ₹48,000 and Loan interest ₹6,000 as charges (Net profit ₹26,000) [2 Marks]. IOC (₹1,00,000) and Salary (₹24,000) exceed available profit; distributed in claims ratio [2.5 Marks]. Partners' Capital Accounts [1.5 Marks].

questions.stem: The partnership deed of X, Y, and Z provided that: (i) Profits be shared in 3:2:1; (ii) IOC @ 9% p.a.; (iii) Salary to Y ₹20,000 p.a.; (iv) X is entitled to 10% commission on net profit before charging commission; (v) Z is entitled to 10% commission on net profit after charging all commissions. Profit before any appropriation was ₹1,80,000. Total capital was ₹6,00,000 in 3:2:1. Prepare P&L Appropriation Account.
questions.correctAnswer: X Commission: ₹18,000; Z Commission: ₹14,727; Divisible profit distributed
questions.rubric: IOC calculation on proportional capitals [1.5 Marks]. X commission @ 10% before charging [1 Mark]. Remaining profit calculation and Z commission @ 10/110 [1.5 Marks]. Net divisible profit split in 3:2:1 [2 Marks].

questions.stem: A, B, and C were partners with Fixed Capitals of ₹5,00,000, ₹3,00,000, and ₹2,00,000 sharing profits in 3:2:1. For the year ended 31st March 2025, Net Profit was ₹1,80,000 before considering: (i) Interest on Capital @ 10% p.a.; (ii) Commission to A @ 10% on Net Profit after charging all commissions and partner salaries; (iii) Salary to B of ₹2,500 p.m. In addition, C had taken a loan of ₹1,00,000 from the firm on 1st October 2024 on which interest was agreed @ 8% p.a. Books were closed without any of these adjustments. Pass a single rectifying journal entry showing detailed working notes.
questions.correctAnswer: Adjusting Journal Entry passed through Current Accounts: B Dr. ₹8,000, C Dr. ₹2,000 to A Cr. ₹10,000
questions.rubric: Interest on C's loan to firm = ₹1,00,000 × 8% × 6/12 = ₹4,000 (Income, net profit becomes ₹1,84,000) [1 Mark]. IOC = ₹1,00,000; Salary B = ₹30,000 [1 Mark]. Balance profit before commission = ₹1,84,000 - ₹1,30,000 = ₹54,000. A's Commission = 54,000 × 10/110 = ₹4,909 [1.5 Marks]. Net divisible profit ₹49,091 split in 3:2:1 [1 Mark]. Analytical adjustment table and single journal entry through Current Accounts [1.5 Marks].

questions.stem: A and B are partners sharing profits in 3:2. On 31st March 2025, after final accounts had been prepared, it was found that Interest on Drawings had been charged @ 12% p.a. instead of 10% p.a. Drawings were: A ₹60,000 and B ₹40,000 (dates not specified). In addition, partner salary to A of ₹12,000 was omitted. Show analytical table and pass a single rectifying journal entry.
questions.correctAnswer: B's Capital A/c Dr. ₹4,400 to A's Capital A/c ₹4,400
questions.rubric: Excess IOD (2% for 6 months): A ₹600, B ₹400 credited back to partners [2 Marks]. Omitted salary credited to A [1.5 Marks]. Total net adjustment redistributed in 3:2 [1.5 Marks]. Single journal entry with narration [1 Mark].

questions.stem: R, S, and T entered into partnership on 1st April 2024 contributing ₹10,00,000, ₹6,00,000, and ₹4,00,000. Terms: (i) IOC @ 6% p.a.; (ii) T guaranteed minimum profit of ₹50,000 p.a. by R and S in 3:1; (iii) R guaranteed that firm fees earned by him will be ₹1,00,000 (actual ₹70,000); (iv) S is entitled to 10% commission on net profit after charging all commissions and guarantees. Net profit before adjustments was ₹2,10,000. Prepare Profit & Loss Appropriation Account.
questions.correctAnswer: P&L Appropriation Account layout balancing at ₹2,40,000 with multi-tier settlements
questions.rubric: R's fee deficiency ₹30,000 credited to P&L App [1.5 Marks]. IOC deduction [1 Mark]. Commission calculation on adjusted profits [1.5 Marks]. T guarantee shortfall recovery from R and S in 3:1 [1.5 Marks]. Final balancing [0.5 Mark].

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding the nature of Goodwill?
options: (a) It is a fictitious asset with no realizable value
(b) It is a tangible asset that can be depreciated over time
(c) It is an intangible asset capable of realizing value on transfer
(d) It is a current asset recorded under cash equivalents
questions.correctAnswer: (c) It is an intangible asset capable of realizing value on transfer
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Goodwill is an intangible asset (not fictitious) because it fetches real consideration on the sale of a business.

questions.stem: According to Accounting Standard 26 (AS-26) issued by ICAI, which form of goodwill can be recognized and recorded in the books of accounts?
options: (a) Internally generated goodwill based on partner consensus
(b) Only purchased goodwill where consideration in money/money's worth is paid
(c) Self-generated goodwill calculated under Super Profit method
(d) Revalued goodwill at the time of reconstitution of partnership
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Only purchased goodwill where consideration in money/money's worth is paid
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. AS-26 permits only purchased goodwill to be capitalized; internally generated goodwill cannot be recognized.

questions.stem: While calculating normal maintainable business profit for goodwill valuation, an abnormal gain arising from profit on sale of machinery must be:
options: (a) Added to that year's net profit
(b) Deducted from that year's net profit
(c) Ignored as it is an asset transaction
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Deducted from that year's net profit
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Non-operating/abnormal gains are deducted to arrive at regular future maintainable business earnings.

questions.stem: If closing stock of the financial year 2023-24 was overvalued by ₹20,000, what is its net correcting effect on the profits of 2023-24 and 2024-25 while valuing goodwill?
options: (c) Deducted from 2023-24 with no effect on 2024-25
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Deducted from 2023-24 and Added to 2024-25
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Overvalued closing stock overstates current profit (deducted in 2023-24) and overstates next year's opening stock, understating 2024-25 profit (added back in 2024-25).

questions.stem: Which of the following assets is strictly EXCLUDED while computing 'Capital Employed' from the asset side?
options: (b) Plant and Machinery in active operation
(d) Closing Stock and Cash at Bank
questions.correctAnswer: (c) Non-trade Investments and Existing Goodwill
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Non-trade investments, existing goodwill, and fictitious assets are strictly excluded from Capital Employed.

questions.stem: Under which method of goodwill valuation is the 'Weighted Average Profit' method considered most suitable?
options: (a) When past profits fluctuate erratically every year
(b) When past profits show a continuous rising or falling trend
(c) When the firm is running at persistent operational losses
(d) When normal rate of return is unknown
questions.correctAnswer: (b) When past profits show a continuous rising or falling trend
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Weighted average assigns higher weight to recent years when profits exhibit a clear secular trend.

questions.stem: Super Profit is defined as the excess of:
options: (a) Normal profit over actual average maintainable profit
(b) Actual average maintainable profit over normal profit
(d) Capital employed over total outside liabilities
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Actual average maintainable profit over normal profit
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Super Profit = Average Maintainable Profit - Normal Profit.

questions.stem: On 1st October 2023, a major overhaul of plant worth ₹40,000 was wrongly debited to Repairs Account. Depreciation is charged @ 10% p.a. on Straight Line Method. What adjustment is required in the profit of 2023-24?
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Add ₹40,000 and Deduct ₹2,000
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Add back capital expense wrongly treated as revenue (+₹40,000) and deduct depreciation for 6 months: 40,000 × 10% × 6/12 = -₹2,000.

questions.stem: If Capital Employed is ₹5,00,000, Normal Rate of Return is 10%, and Goodwill valued under Capitalisation of Super Profit is ₹1,00,000, the Super Profit must be:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Goodwill = (Super Profit / NRR) × 100. Thus, Super Profit = 1,00,000 × 10% = ₹10,000.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Capitalisation of Average Profit method and Capitalisation of Super Profit method always yield the identical value of goodwill.
Reason (R): Both methods mathematically measure the capitalized value of the business earnings in excess of net assets employed at the normal rate of return.
options: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
(d) A is false but R is true
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Both capitalization formulas yield identical results when applied to identical underlying balance sheet figures.

questions.stem: Firm's profit for 2024 was ₹80,000 including interest of ₹8,000 from 8% non-trade investments of ₹1,00,000. For valuing goodwill, the adjusted profit of 2024 will be:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Income from non-trade investments (₹8,000) does not belong to main operating business and must be deducted: 80,000 - 8,000 = ₹72,000.

questions.stem: A firm has Total Assets of ₹12,00,000 and Outside Creditors of ₹3,00,000. It earned an average profit of ₹1,20,000. If the normal rate of return is 10%, the value of goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profit is:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Net Assets = 12L - 3L = ₹9,00,000. Capitalized Value = 1,20,000 / 10% = ₹12,00,000. Goodwill = 12L - 9L = ₹3,00,000.

questions.stem:
Statement I: Undervaluation of closing stock in 2023 results in understating the true profit of 2023.
Statement II: Undervaluation of opening stock in 2024 results in overstating the true profit of 2024.
options: (c) Statement I is true, Statement II is false
(d) Statement I is false, Statement II is true
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Both statements are true
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Undervalued closing stock lowers trading credit (understates profit). Undervalued opening stock lowers debit (overstates profit).

questions.stem: If a partner's fair annual remuneration of ₹30,000 has not been deducted while determining past profits, how is it treated for goodwill valuation?
options: (a) Deducted from Average Maintainable Profit as an expected operational charge
(b) Ignored because it is an appropriation of profit
(d) Deducted from Normal Rate of Return
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Deducted from Average Maintainable Profit as an expected operational charge
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Fair remuneration to partners is treated as an operating cost to determine future maintainable business earnings.

questions.stem: When purchase consideration paid for an ongoing business is ₹15,00,000 while fair market value of net tangible assets taken over is ₹13,20,000, the differential ₹1,80,000 represents:
questions.correctAnswer: (b) Purchased Goodwill
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Excess of purchase consideration over net identifiable tangible assets is Purchased Goodwill debited to Goodwill Account.

questions.stem: Calculate goodwill of a firm on the basis of 3 years' purchase of average profits of the last 4 years. Profits were: 2021-22: ₹80,000 (including abnormal gain of ₹10,000); 2022-23: ₹1,00,000 (after charging abnormal loss of ₹20,000); 2023-24: ₹90,000; 2024-25: ₹1,10,000 (excluding ₹10,000 insurance premium of firm property now to be paid annually).
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹2,85,000

questions.stem: A and B are partners. Firm's past profits were: 2022-23: ₹1,40,000; 2023-24: ₹1,60,000; 2024-25: ₹2,10,000. An audit revealed that: (i) Profit of 2022-23 included profit on sale of investments ₹20,000; (ii) In 2023-24, plant was destroyed by fire resulting in loss of ₹30,000 debited to P&L; (iii) Partners are entitled to annual remuneration of ₹25,000 each which was not deducted. Calculate goodwill at 2 years' purchase of average profits.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹2,40,000

questions.stem: On 1st October 2023, a major repair of machinery costing ₹60,000 was charged to Revenue. Depreciation is charged @ 20% p.a. on Diminishing Balance Method. The book profits were: 2023-24: ₹1,80,000 and 2024-25: ₹2,20,000. Calculate corrected profits for both years.

Profits of a firm for the last three years were: 2022-23: ₹90,000; 2023-24: ₹1,20,000; 2024-25: ₹1,50,000. Closing stock for 2023-24 was overvalued by ₹15,000. Calculate goodwill on the basis of 2 years' purchase of average profit of the last 3 years.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹2,40,000

questions.stem: Calculate goodwill of a firm under Weighted Average Profit method based on 3 years' purchase. Profits: 2021-22: ₹40,000; 2022-23: ₹48,000; 2023-24: ₹60,000; 2024-25: ₹72,000. Weights assigned: 1, 2, 3, 4 respectively. An annual management charge of ₹6,000 was omitted in all years.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹1,60,800

questions.stem: A firm earned average profits of ₹1,50,000 during the last few years. Total assets were ₹14,00,000 and outside liabilities were ₹4,00,000. The normal rate of return in this industry is 10%. Calculate goodwill by 3 years' purchase of Super Profit.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹1,50,000

questions.stem: Capital accounts of partners A and B stood at ₹4,00,000 and ₹3,00,000 alongside General Reserve of ₹1,00,000. Balance Sheet assets included ₹50,000 in Non-trade investments. Normal rate of return is 12%. Firm's average profit is ₹1,10,000 (including ₹5,000 interest from non-trade investments). Calculate goodwill at 2 years' purchase of super profit.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹30,000
questions.rubric: Capital Employed = (4L + 3L + 1L) - Non-trade 50k = ₹7,50,000 [1 Mark]. Normal Profit = 7,50,000 × 12% = ₹90,000 [0.5 Mark]. Average Maintainable Profit = 1,10,000 - 5,000 = ₹1,05,000 [0.5 Mark]. Super Profit = ₹15,000; Goodwill = 15,000 × 2 = ₹30,000 [1 Mark].

questions.stem: A firm has an average maintainable profit of ₹80,000. Total tangible assets are ₹9,00,000 and outside liabilities are ₹3,00,000. Normal rate of return is 10%. Calculate the value of goodwill under Capitalisation of Average Profit Method.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹2,00,000
questions.rubric: Capitalized Value of Business = (80,000 / 10) × 100 = ₹8,00,000 [1.5 Marks]. Net Assets (Capital Employed) = 9,00,000 - 3,00,000 = ₹6,00,000 [1 Mark]. Goodwill = 8,00,000 - 6,00,000 = ₹2,00,000 [0.5 Mark].

questions.stem: Capitals of X and Y are ₹3,50,000 and ₹2,50,000. P&L A/c showed a credit balance of ₹60,000 and Sundry Creditors were ₹1,40,000. Normal rate of return is 10%. Average profit earned is ₹85,000. Calculate goodwill under Capitalisation of Super Profit Method.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹1,90,000

questions.stem: A firm earned profits of ₹1,00,000. Capital employed in the business is ₹8,00,000 and the normal rate of return is 10%. Calculate goodwill by: (i) Capitalisation of Average Profit Method, and (ii) Capitalisation of Super Profit Method. Prove that both methods result in the identical figure.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill by both methods = ₹2,00,000
questions.rubric: (i) Capitalized Value = 1,00,000/10% = ₹10,00,000; Goodwill = 10L - 8L = ₹2,00,000 [1.5 Marks]. (ii) Normal Profit = ₹80,000; Super Profit = ₹20,000; Goodwill = 20,000/10% = ₹2,00,000 [1.5 Marks].

questions.stem: Goodwill of a firm is valued at ₹1,20,000 at 3 years' purchase of super profit. If capital employed by the firm is ₹6,00,000 and the normal rate of return is 10%, calculate the actual average profit of the firm.
questions.correctAnswer: Actual Average Profit = ₹1,00,000
questions.rubric: Super Profit = Goodwill / 3 = 1,20,000 / 3 = ₹40,000 [1 Mark]. Normal Profit = 6,00,000 × 10% = ₹60,000 [1 Mark]. Actual Average Profit = Normal Profit + Super Profit = 60,000 + 40,000 = ₹1,00,000 [1 Mark].

questions.stem: Under Capitalisation of Average Profit Method, goodwill of a firm was valued at ₹1,60,000. Average profit of the firm is ₹72,000 and the normal rate of return is 12%. Calculate the Capital Employed (Net Assets) of the business.
questions.correctAnswer: Capital Employed = ₹4,40,000
questions.rubric: Total Capitalized Value = (72,000 / 12) × 100 = ₹6,00,000 [1.5 Marks]. Goodwill = Capitalized Value - Net Assets. Thus, Net Assets = 6,00,000 - 1,60,000 = ₹4,40,000 [1.5 Marks].

questions.stem: A partnership firm has Capital of ₹5,00,000, General Reserve of ₹1,50,000, and Debit balance in P&L Account of ₹50,000. Normal rate of return is 10%. Average profit earned is ₹90,000, but a fair partner salary of ₹10,000 p.a. has not been provided. Calculate goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹60,000
questions.rubric: Capital Employed = 5,00,000 + 1,50,000 - 50,000 (accumulated loss) = ₹6,00,000 [1 Mark]. Normal Profit = 6,00,000 × 10% = ₹60,000 [0.5 Mark]. Average Maintainable Profit = 90,000 - 10,000 = ₹80,000 [0.5 Mark]. Super Profit = ₹20,000; Goodwill = 20,000 × 3 = ₹60,000 [1 Mark].

questions.stem: Profits for the last 3 years were: 2022-23: ₹1,00,000; 2023-24: ₹1,50,000; 2024-25: ₹1,80,000. Adjustments: (i) Undervaluation of closing stock in 2023-24 by ₹10,000; (ii) Loss on sale of obsolete equipment in 2022-23 of ₹15,000; (iii) Recurring management charge of ₹12,000 p.a. not charged. Calculate goodwill on 2 years' purchase of average profit.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹2,66,000

questions.stem: Balance Sheet showed: Total Assets ₹11,50,000 (which includes Existing Goodwill of ₹50,000 and Fictitious Asset of ₹20,000). Outside Liabilities were ₹2,80,000. Average maintainable profit is ₹1,20,000 and NRR is 12%. Value the goodwill of the firm under Capitalisation of Average Profit Method.
questions.correctAnswer: Goodwill = ₹2,00,000

chapters.chapterName: Reconstitution of Partnership: Change in Profit Sharing Ratio

questions.stem: Sacrificing ratio is calculated at the time of change in profit sharing ratio among existing partners as:
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Old Share - New Share
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Sacrificing Ratio = Old Profit Share - New Profit Share.

questions.stem: When a new partner brings his share of goodwill in cash, it is credited to:
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Premium for Goodwill Account
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Cash brought for goodwill is credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c.

chapters.chapterName: Retirement and Death of a Partner

questions.stem: Gaining ratio is calculated on the retirement of a partner as:
questions.correctAnswer: (a) New Share - Old Share
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Gaining Ratio = New Share - Old Share.

questions.stem: On dissolution of a firm, unrecorded assets when realized are credited to:
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Realisation Account
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Proceeds of unrecorded assets are credited to Realisation A/c.

questions.stem: Maximum rate of interest allowed on Calls-in-Arrears as per Table F of the Companies Act, 2013 is:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. As per Table F, max interest on calls-in-arrears is 10% p.a.

questions.stem: Discount on issue of debentures is written off as per AS-16 in the year of issue from:
options: (a) Securities Premium Account / Statement of Profit and Loss
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Securities Premium Account / Statement of Profit and Loss
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Written off from Securities Premium A/c first, then P&L.

questions.stem: As per Schedule III Part I of Companies Act, 2013, 'Unpaid Dividend' is shown under:
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Other Current Liabilities
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Unpaid dividend is classified under Other Current Liabilities.

questions.stem: Horizontal analysis of financial statements is also known as:
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Dynamic Analysis
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Horizontal analysis compares data over multiple years (Dynamic).

questions.stem: Ideal Current Ratio recommended for a commercial business firm is:
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Ideal Current Ratio is 2 : 1.

questions.stem: Under AS-3, dividend paid by a financing company is classified under:
questions.correctAnswer: (a) Financing Activities
questions.rubric: 1 Mark. Dividend paid is always a Financing Activity for all companies.
